Hi, happy new year! I have something new in my shop. I made similar ones for ladies in my life who have supported my heart through 2023. If you’re interested in this or my horses there’s lots in my shop and I’m working on a couple more of these pouches with different mending techniques and stitches on the hearts

Thread. This horse and several others were made from my grandad’s shirts my dad inherited until they wore out. They were all individuals with added labels here and there and I let my niece and nephews choose from a selection and my parents have one each too. There’s so much sentimental significance held in these threads, memories of my grandad, dad and family times we shared and saw them being worn. #seamcollective #seamcollective23 @seam_collective

I’m influenced and inspired by nature and led by my materials and thread shades. I use various stitches, simple running stitch is my favourite. I began stitching properly when I discovered Sashiko, a running stitch in different directions that construct not only a beautiful aesthetic but also a strong and reconstructive quality. Most of my work then was based on Sashiko. I learned a lot through it to mend and repair different materials. The last year I’ve been making lots of little horses, all unique and quirky. My favourite way to work is with leftover or preloved materials and figuring ways to use them, the process is experimental and I usually have no clue how it will look when it’s finished. As most makers find, the joy is more in the process than the result, stitching is meditative and intuitive for me, a slow pace, a rhythm and my hands and brain enjoy it. @seam_collective #septtextilelove #septtextilelove23

Hi, I’m Emilie. I collect fabrics, old and new and make them into patches, horses and jewellery. I started properly in 2016 when I discovered Sashiko. I lived in Beijing and began doing markets like this from 2017, I sold my embroidered wares and did live mending. I did workshops from home and in collaboration with a zero waste company in Beijing. Since then lots has happened, including having a baby and unexpectedly relocating back to the UK. I’m currently in south west England where I continue to see most days, it keeps my hands busy and helps my sanity.
